low_cost_ai.existing: Curated hints work with AI off. The desktop supports optional Ollama and a personal Claude API key.
low_cost_ai.required: Provide an inexpensive or free assistance and grading mechanism. Define its evidence, rubric, model limits, and relationship to actual code-test results.
low_cost_ai.implementation: AI review makes at most one explicit request to the selected provider. A prerequisite error or cancellation can prevent inference. Coding uses four criteria. Design uses six brief criteria and creates a checkpoint. Numeric scores from zero to three require a quotation found in captured code, notes, or diagram labels. Null means the evidence is not sufficient. The app supplies a fixed practice question for the selected criterion. It rejects new model prose, duplicate JSON fields, unknown criteria, invalid scores, tool requests, and cancelled late answers. It does not run tests or complete practice.
low_cost_ai.state: The result identifies its attempt/code hash or checkpoint/scene hash. It stays in the captured conversation with the previous 200-record limit and file format. Draft autosave continues during inference. Curated reviews, test results, progress, and completion keep their previous meaning. AI stays off by default.
low_cost_ai.limits: Each request contains at most 20000 UTF-8 evidence bytes, excluding system instructions and the JSON schema. Ollama uses a 32768-token context. Output has a 1500-token maximum. There are no automatic retries. Local Ollama has no API charge. The Claude provider uses the user's paid account.

design_completion_story.evidence: The new native story passed in 5.4 seconds. It uses real renderer controls, preload, service, backend, and saved practice data. An IPC gate supplies one controlled failure before the backend call. It checks duplicate clicks, unchanged attempt after failure, retry, completion, restart, locked notes, and a fresh attempt that preserves the completed record. The independent review requested stronger duplicate-count and canvas assertions. The updated native story passed, including unchanged saved notes/canvas and an empty canvas for the new attempt.
design_completion_story.limits: The injected failure occurs before the backend completion call. It does not cover a backend commit followed by a local state write failure.

sandbox_close_cancellation.behavior: A native close request cancels the active sandbox command before the renderer waits for active work. The manager creates a new cancellation controller after the operation ends, so a failed draft save can permit another inspection. Final shutdown still validates ownership before stopping containers.
sandbox_close_cancellation.evidence: Before the fix, the native test failed its five-second close check while Docker --version waited for its ten-second timeout. After the fix, the story passed in 2.5 seconds. All 11 related native stories passed. All 245 desktop unit/process tests passed with 2 optional skips. The build passed.
sandbox_close_cancellation.scope: The native fixture replaces Docker with a temporary Linux executable. It does not start or stop a real container. The manager unit test verifies inspection after cancellation. Native close during image/runtime installation and final owned-container cleanup remains to be tested.
sandbox_close_cancellation.data_effect: Draft-save checks and saved data formats have no changes. A failed save still prevents closure.
sandbox_close_cancellation.review_corrections: The independent review found queued commands, accepted actions that reached the backend after closure began, and cancelled runtime reads that could trigger container startup. A cancellation generation now rejects older queued work. The close gate rejects new sandbox commands but permits draft saves. Cancelled runtime reads reject, and cancelled commands cannot reach the command runner.
sandbox_close_cancellation.latest_checks: The build and 16 sandbox unit tests passed. All 9 native close stories passed, including coding/settings/design/queue save failures, close retry, timer/input behavior, and both delayed and active sandbox requests.
sandbox_close_cancellation.consent_correction: An accepted sandbox-enable request can wait in the consent dialog. The handler now checks closure again after consent returns and before setup starts. A native held-consent test failed its five-second close check before the fix and passed after it. The three shutdown cases and three distribution stories passed together in 14.5 seconds.

distribution_stories.coverage: Configured update controls retain the beta channel, reject duplicate clicks, disable other controls during work, show check/download/installer errors, and permit explicit retry. signed_update_native_story.mechanism: The test compiles the real source bundle with one temporary release public key. It supplies signed fixture responses through fetch and intercepts the native confirmation and installer launch. signed_update_native_story.coverage: The story rejects an invalid signature, removes a corrupt download, permits retry, preserves practice after confirmation cancellation, blocks installer launch after backup-directory failure, and retries after that error. At installer-open time, the fixture reads the backup and verifies the saved attempt.
signed_update_native_story.checks: Seven combined native distribution and shutdown stories passed in 17.5 seconds. The final backup-at-open assertion passed in a focused native run. Type checks and formatting passed.
signed_update_native_story.limits: The source fixture uses a temporary release public key and skips packaged executables. The separate update-close story covers metadata, download, consent, and cached-file verification cancellation.

update_close_cancellation.behavior: Native close cancels metadata fetches, streamed downloads, and cached installer verification. The close gate rejects new update actions. The install handler checks closure after verification, after confirmation, and before installer opening. Cancelled operations release the busy state and permit explicit retry if closure fails.
